q2_gaps: a PLURAL collective noun with a member-kind of-phrase ("large herds of cows") — the instruction set covers only the singular "a flock of birds" (Member + GroupOf) and gives no form for a group whose members are themselves groups, nor for placing a GroupOf atom inside a distribution rule's conclusion
notes: Demonstrative plural to a group witness, "had" to Holder/Theme with Past, and "large" distributed to each herd (not to the cows) all follow the instruction set. The possession predicate gets no per-member distribution rule over the Tuareg group — defensible as a collective reading, though the plural/distributive rule would otherwise call for one since "have" is not a collective predicate.
